content.text: A **truth table** lists every way the letters can be true (T) or false (F), and works out the formula on each row.

content.definition: True on every row, like P ∨ ¬P.
False on every row, like P ∧ ¬P.
True on some rows and false on others.

examples.title: And
lines: P is T, Q is T: P ∧ Q is T
P is T, Q is F: P ∧ Q is F
P is F, Q is T: P ∧ Q is F
P is F, Q is F: P ∧ Q is F
examples.note: ∧ is true only when both parts are true.

examples.title: If then
lines: P is T, Q is T: P → Q is T
P is T, Q is F: P → Q is F
P is F, Q is T: P → Q is T
P is F, Q is F: P → Q is T
examples.note: → is false only when P is true and Q is false.

examples.title: Or
lines: P is T, Q is T: P ∨ Q is T
P is T, Q is F: P ∨ Q is T
P is F, Q is T: P ∨ Q is T
P is F, Q is F: P ∨ Q is F
examples.note: ∨ is false only when both parts are false.

question.hint: Try P true, then P false. Which formula is true both times?
question.explanation: P ∨ ¬P is true whether P is true or false, so it is true on every row.
